1.explanation:
1. audits/short-name-length-test.js: Contains the unit tests for the short_name length audit; you’ll want to see how missing values are handled and what the expected behavior is.  
2. audits/short-name-test.js: Tests the presence and basic processing of the short_name field; comparing it against the length test helps understand the audit chain.  
3. audits/exists-test.js: A generic “exists” audit for manifest properties—examines how missing properties are detected and reported.  
4. gather/gatherers/manifest-test.js: Validates how the manifest gatherer reads and outputs the manifest artifact, including how undefined or missing short_name is represented.  
5. lib/manifest-parser-test.js: Exercises the parser logic that normalizes manifest fields (including defaulting missing fields), which directly impacts what value gets passed to the length audit.
1.bug_scenario: The Lighthouse audit “short-name-length” is incorrectly flagging a missing short_name in the web app manifest as a zero‐character label and raising a warning (“12 chars is the suggested maximum homescreen label length (Found: 0 chars)”). In other words, when the manifest’s short_name field is absent, the audit still measures its length as 0 and reports a length violation instead of treating it as “missing” or passing the check. The screenshot shows the red warning line under the audit title, indicating a 0-char label length against the 12-char recommendation.
